title: From Inspiral to Outburst: Modeling a Potential Luminous Red Nova from Betelgeuse
summary: Recent evidence suggests that Betelgeuse may host a stellar companion whose orbit will decay through tidal interactions, ultimately leading to engulfment and merger within the next several thousand years. If confirmed, this system could represent the nearest and best-characterized progenitor of a future luminous red nova (LRN). We investigate whether the shock-breakout and cooling emission preceding the LRN can be used to constrain the properties of the companion and its disruption within the stellar envelope. Using binary stellar evolution calculations, we evolve Betelgeuse with companions of $0.7$, $1.0$, and $2.0 M_\odot$ to the onset of common envelope evolution (CEE). We then perform one-dimensional radiation-hydrodynamic simulations that follow companion disruption, energy deposition, and shock propagation through the envelope. We find that the peak luminosity increases systematically with companion mass, from $2.44\times10^{41}$ to $6.17\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ across the $0.7$-$2.0 M_\odot$ models, while the duration increases more modestly from $1.48$ to $1.99$ days and attains apparent magnitudes brighter than Venus as viewed from Earth. Tidal disruption contributes both kinetic energy and mass to the envelope, linking the companion's structure and mass to the energetics of the shock-heated ejecta. The monotonic luminosity sequence demonstrates that the early breakout emission can retain direct information about the engulfed companion. The interaction ejects $6.15$-$11.19 M_\odot$ of hydrogen-rich material, substantially modifying both the envelope structure and circumstellar environment prior to core collapse.

AI.tldr: Betelgeuse's putative stellar companion will be engulfed within a few thousand years, and the pre-merger shock-breakout and cooling emission can be used to infer the companion's mass, with peak luminosity scaling monotonically from 2.44 to 6.17×10^41 erg/s for companions of 0.7–2.0 M_sun.
AI.motivation: Recent evidence suggests Betelgeuse may host a companion whose orbit decays via tides, leading to engulfment and merger within several thousand years, potentially making it the nearest, best-characterized progenitor of a luminous red nova (LRN). The authors ask whether the shock-breakout and cooling emission preceding the LRN can constrain the companion's properties and its disruption within the stellar envelope.
AI.method: Binary stellar evolution calculations evolve Betelgeuse with 0.7, 1.0, and 2.0 M_sun companions up to the onset of common envelope evolution (CEE). One-dimensional radiation-hydrodynamic simulations then follow companion disruption, energy deposition, and shock propagation through the envelope.
AI.result: Peak luminosity increases systematically with companion mass (2.44×10^41 to 6.17×10^41 erg/s across 0.7–2.0 M_sun), while duration rises modestly from 1.48 to 1.99 days; the events reach apparent magnitudes brighter than Venus as seen from Earth. Tidal disruption supplies both kinetic energy and mass to the envelope, tying companion structure and mass to the energetics of the shock-heated ejecta. The interaction ejects 6.15–11.19 M_sun of hydrogen-rich material, substantially modifying the envelope structure and circumstellar environment before core collapse.
AI.conclusion: The monotonic luminosity sequence shows that early breakout emission retains direct information about the engulfed companion, making pre-LRN shock-breakout/cooling emission a viable diagnostic of companion mass and disruption, and establishing this system as a well-characterized future LRN progenitor whose pre-collapse ejecta reshape the envelope and circumstellar medium.

title: FastSpec: Fast and versatile stellar spectrum synthesis code
comment: 15 pages, 11 figures: Astronomy & Astrophysics, in press
summary: Modelling data from modern spectroscopic surveys and time-resolved spectropolarimetric observations requires stellar synthetic spectra to be computed rapidly over wide wavelength ranges from line lists that increasingly reach hundreds of millions of transitions. Spectropolarimetric analyses of magnetically active stars additionally demand a solution of the polarised radiative transfer problem. We present FastSpec, a new LTE spectrum synthesis code designed around two goals: increased raw computational speed and broad astrophysical applicability, including the calculation of the full Stokes vector in the presence of a magnetic field. FastSpec computes emergent intensity and flux spectra from plane-parallel and spherical model atmospheres. Chemical and ionisation equilibrium is obtained from the updated SME equation-of-state package, continuum opacities follow the ATLAS family of routines, hydrogen bound-bound and bound-free absorption uses the occupation-probability formalism, and line absorption is evaluated with fast table-based Voigt and Faraday-Voigt profile algorithms. The transfer equation is integrated with DELO-Bezier formal solvers in both scalar and Stokes-vector form. Speed is achieved through aggressive OpenMP parallelisation, adaptive per-line wavelength windowing, and a memory-capped block-processing scheme that lets arbitrarily large line lists be handled within a user-defined RAM budget. The code synthesises spectra thousands of Å wide from line lists of $10^8$ molecular and atomic transitions in under a minute on a modern multi-core laptop while reproducing benchmark calculations from established codes. FastSpec combines the physical completeness of classical model atmosphere and spectrum synthesis codes with the speed required by large surveys and the polarised transfer needed for stellar magnetism studies into a single portable package.

AI.tldr: FastSpec is a new LTE spectrum synthesis code that rapidly computes intensity and full Stokes-vector spectra from line lists of 10^8 transitions in under a minute on a multi-core laptop.
AI.motivation: Modern spectroscopic surveys and time-resolved spectropolarimetry require synthetic spectra computed rapidly over wide wavelength ranges from line lists reaching hundreds of millions of transitions. Analyses of magnetically active stars additionally require solving the polarised radiative transfer problem.
AI.method: FastSpec computes emergent intensity and flux from plane-parallel and spherical atmospheres. It uses the SME equation-of-state package for chemical/ionisation equilibrium, ATLAS-family continuum opacities, occupation-probability formalism for hydrogen bound-bound and bound-free absorption, and fast table-based Voigt and Faraday-Voigt line profiles. The transfer equation is integrated with DELO-Bezier formal solvers in scalar and Stokes-vector form. Speed comes from aggressive OpenMP parallelisation, adaptive per-line wavelength windowing, and a memory-capped block-processing scheme handling arbitrarily large line lists within a user-defined RAM budget.
AI.result: The code synthesises spectra thousands of Å wide from line lists of 10^8 molecular and atomic transitions in under a minute on a modern multi-core laptop, while reproducing benchmark calculations from established codes.
AI.conclusion: FastSpec unifies the physical completeness of classical model atmosphere and spectrum synthesis codes with the speed demanded by large surveys and the polarised transfer required for stellar magnetism studies, all in a single portable package.

title: Probing Red Giant Interiors with g-Dominated Mixed Modes II: The Cases of KIC 6117517, KIC 9475697, KIC 10123207 and KIC 10200377
comment: 28 pages, 15 figures, 14 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Building on Paper~I, which constrained core overshooting to $f_{\rm ov} < 0.01$ for $M < 1.4\,M_{\odot}$ and found $α_{\rm MLT} \simeq 2.0$ for metal-rich red giants, we extend this analysis to four lower-mass \textit{Kepler} red giants spanning a broad metallicity range: KIC~6117517, KIC~9475697, KIC~10123207, and KIC~10200377. Two complementary model grids are constructed: Grid~A fixes $α_{\rm MLT} = 2.0$ while varying metallicity; Grid~B adopts spectroscopic metallicities with $α_{\rm MLT}$ as a free parameter. Grid~A successfully reproduces both asteroseismic and spectroscopic constraints for the metal-rich targets (KIC~6117517 and KIC~9475697), confirming $α_{\rm MLT} = 2.0$ for metal-rich red giants. For the metal-poor targets (KIC~10123207 and KIC~10200377), Grid~B yields larger mixing-length parameters of $α_{\rm MLT} \approx 2.16$--$2.18$. Although only four stars are analyzed with unequal sensitivity to $α_{\rm MLT}$, these results suggest a tentative increase in convective efficiency toward lower metallicity, consistent with 3D hydrodynamical simulations but opposite to some 1D empirical calibrations. The best-fitting overshooting parameters ($f_{\rm ov} = 0.006$--$0.007$) independently support the Paper~I constraint and are consistent with a mass-dependent overshooting relation. The parameter uncertainties reach $0.6$--$2.5\%$ in mass, $0.2$--$0.9\%$ in radius, $2$--$13\%$ in age, and below $0.6\%$ in helium-core mass and below $0.2\%$ in helium-core radius. Surface-effect corrections are negligible for g-dominated mixed modes, validating $χ^2_{l=1g}$ as a robust fitting metric. For KIC~9475697, the core rotation rate is determined to be $Ω_{\rm core} = 0.6945 \pm 0.0190\,μ$Hz from model-based trapping parameters.

AI.tldr: Extended asteroseismic modeling of four low-mass Kepler red giants favors α_MLT ≈ 2.0 for metal-rich stars and slightly higher (~2.16–2.18) for metal-poor ones, with small overshooting (f_ov ≈ 0.006–0.007).
AI.motivation: Paper I constrained core overshooting (f_ov < 0.01) and mixing-length parameter (α_MLT ≈ 2.0) for metal-rich red giants with M < 1.4 M_sun. This work tests whether these calibrations hold for lower-mass red giants across a broad metallicity range and probes the metallicity dependence of convective efficiency.
AI.method: Two model grids were built for four Kepler red giants (KIC 6117517, 9475697, 10123207, 10200377): Grid A fixes α_MLT = 2.0 and varies metallicity; Grid B uses spectroscopic metallicities with α_MLT free. Fits combine asteroseismic and spectroscopic constraints, using χ²_{l=1g} as the metric, with surface-effect checks and model-based mixed-mode trapping parameters.
AI.result: Grid A reproduces metal-rich targets (KIC 6117517, 9475697) with α_MLT = 2.0. Grid B gives α_MLT ≈ 2.16–2.18 for metal-poor targets (KIC 10123207, 10200377). Best-fit f_ov = 0.006–0.007, consistent with Paper I and a mass-dependent overshooting relation. Uncertainties: 0.6–2.5% (mass), 0.2–0.9% (radius), 2–13% (age), <0.6% (He-core mass), <0.2% (He-core radius). Surface effects are negligible for g-dominated modes. For KIC 9475697, Ω_core = 0.6945 ± 0.0190 μHz.
AI.conclusion: Results tentatively indicate increasing convective efficiency toward lower metallicity, consistent with 3D hydrodynamical simulations but opposite to some 1D empirical calibrations. The overshooting constraint is independently confirmed. Caveats include the small sample (four stars) and unequal sensitivity to α_MLT; the metallicity trend remains tentative.

title: A comprehensive reanalysis of HD 99458. Not a magnetic Ap star but an oscillating Algol with ongoing mass transfer
comment: 34 pages, 31 figures, 18 tables (including the full Table A.1.), 3 appendices. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Context. Since 2019, HD 99458 has been known as a unique example of a $δ$ Sct variable with chemical peculiarities of Ap type in an eclipsing binary. Aims. We aim to review the peculiar status of the star with new observational materials. Methods. The current study is the result of meticulous analysis of space-based photometry from Kepler K2 and TESS, multi-site spectroscopic and spectropolarimetric observations, as well as speckle-interferometric data. Asteroseismic modelling of stellar pulsation is an essential part of the research. Results. We find HD 99458 to be an eclipsing Algol-type system with active mass transfer from the cool companion filling its Roche lobe to the pulsating primary. We identified signatures of a disc and accretion with varying rates in spectra and light curves. The system's orbital period increases with the rate $\dot{P}_\mathrm{orb}$ of 5.045 s yr$^{-1}$, indicating potential multiplicity. We failed to detect traces of the primary's magnetic field or excessive abundances, both of which are necessary to classify HD 99458 as an Ap star. We have constrained the fundamental parameters of the pulsating primary and analysed its pulsation using asteroseismology. In space-based photometry, we identified pulsation modes with angular degree $\ell\leq3$. Two-dimensional Fourier analysis of spectroscopic time series reveals pulsations in the form of standing waves with the azimuthal orders $|m|=5\pm1$. Combined analysis of photometry and spectroscopy confirms the status of HD 99458 as a triaxial gravitationally distorted pulsator. Conclusions. Our comprehensive study affirms the new classification for HD 99458.

AI.tldr: New K2/TESS photometry, spectroscopy, spectropolarimetry and asteroseismology show HD 99458 is an Algol-type eclipsing binary with active mass transfer and a tidally distorted δ Sct primary — not the unique Ap-type pulsator previously claimed.
AI.motivation: HD 99458 was previously catalogued as a unique example of a δ Sct pulsator with Ap-type chemical peculiarities residing in an eclipsing binary, a peculiar combination that warranted verification with improved data.
AI.method: Analysis of Kepler K2 and TESS space photometry, multi-site spectroscopy and spectropolarimetry, speckle interferometry, and asteroseismic modelling of the pulsations (including 2D Fourier analysis of spectroscopic time series).
AI.result: HD 99458 is an eclipsing Algol-type system with active mass transfer from the Roche-lobe-filling cool companion onto the pulsating primary; disc and variable accretion signatures appear in spectra and light curves; orbital period increases at 5.045 s/yr, suggesting additional multiplicity. No magnetic field or abundance anomalies were detected, invalidating the Ap classification. Pulsation modes with ℓ≤3 were identified in photometry, and azimuthal orders |m|=5±1 in spectroscopy, confirming a triaxial, gravitationally distorted pulsator.
AI.conclusion: The comprehensive reanalysis establishes a revised classification of HD 99458, replacing its previous unique Ap/δ Sct eclipsing-binary status with that of an Algol-type interacting binary hosting a tidally distorted pulsator.

title: Accuracy of electric current inference assuming three-dimensional hydrostatic equilibrium
summary: The chromospheric and coronal heating problem is among the major open questions in solar physics. Some of the possible mechanisms that can explain the rise in temperature that is needed to reproduce the observations require the estimation of electric currents. Since these depend on the spatial derivatives of the magnetic field components, it is necessary to obtain the full magnetic field vector from observational data in a 3D geometrical grid. We developed a new method to obtain the 3D geometrical configuration of the atmosphere using the approximation of hydrostatic equilibrium in three dimensions to determine the gas pressure and density as a function of optical depth, column mass, or geometrical distance. This development has been designed as an extension for any inversion code that outputs a stratification of temperature and gas pressure or density to enable the estimation of electric current densities from observations. We investigated our approach using a snapshot from a sunspot MHD simulation. The difference between the solver output and the simulation, taken as the ground truth, is mostly between 30 and 45 %, showing a similar pattern over a large optical depth range. Additional tests also showed that the solver provides a unique solution, has a scarce sensitivity to the boundary condition and is only marginally impacted by the viewing angle. We conclude that the electric currents can be inferred at a reasonable accuracy with this approach using the simulation parameters as input. We also tested set-ups that aim at mimicking more realistic cases, where the code performed equally well. The results in this work show promise with respect to future applications to spectropolarimetric data, however, some additional challenges will need to be adressed when moving from the controlled input of the simulation to observational data.

AI.tldr: A 3D geometrical inversion extension recovers the full magnetic field vector stratification under hydrostatic equilibrium assumptions, enabling estimation of electric current densities from spectropolarimetric data with roughly 30–45% accuracy against MHD ground truth.
AI.motivation: Understanding chromospheric and coronal heating in solar physics requires estimating electric current densities, which depend on spatial derivatives of all magnetic field components. This demands the full 3D magnetic field vector on a geometrical grid—something not directly provided by standard inversion codes, which typically output 1D temperature and gas pressure/density stratifications. The paper addresses this gap.
AI.method: The authors develop a method to reconstruct the 3D geometrical configuration of the solar atmosphere by assuming hydrostatic equilibrium in three dimensions, thereby determining gas pressure and density as functions of optical depth, column mass, or geometrical distance. The approach is designed as an extension to any inversion code that outputs temperature and gas pressure/density stratifications, aiming to enable estimation of electric current densities from observations. The method is validated against a sunspot MHD simulation snapshot used as ground truth, with additional tests of solution uniqueness, boundary-condition sensitivity, and viewing-angle dependence, plus more realistic setups.
AI.result: The difference between solver output and the MHD simulation ground truth is mostly 30–45%, with a similar pattern across a large optical depth range. Tests show the solver provides a unique solution, has low sensitivity to boundary conditions, and is only marginally affected by viewing angle. Performance remained acceptable on setups mimicking more realistic cases.
AI.conclusion: Electric currents can be inferred at reasonable accuracy with this approach when using simulation parameters as input. The results are promising for future application to spectropolarimetric data, though additional challenges must be addressed when moving from controlled simulation input to observational data.

title: ARENA: Active Region attENtion Aggregation for interpretable solar flare prediction
comment: 7+12 pages (2+8 figures), accepted at the "Representations for the Physical Sciences" workshop at NeurIPS 2026
summary: Predicting solar flares is a challenging space-weather forecasting problem with potentially significant impacts on Earth's upper atmosphere, including disruptions to radio communications. We propose Active Region attENtion Aggregation (ARENA), a neural network architecture that predicts solar flares from a variable number of active-region cutouts while learning to identify the region most relevant to the prediction. ARENA is trained using multiple-instance learning under weak supervision, requiring only a flare/no-flare label for the observation and no labels specifying the flare origin. The learned attention mechanism therefore provides a means of localizing the active region driving the prediction without explicit origin annotations. ARENA achieves a heidke skill score of 0.45 which is comparable to other flare prediction approaches. These results demonstrate that active-region-based aggregation can provide an efficient and interpretable approach to solar flare prediction. The code is available at https://github.com/LuisBauer22/ARENA.

AI.tldr: ARENA is an attention-based multiple-instance learning model that predicts solar flares from a variable number of active-region cutouts while localizing the responsible region under weak supervision.
AI.motivation: Solar flare prediction is a challenging space-weather forecasting problem that can disrupt Earth's upper atmosphere and radio communications. Existing approaches typically require explicit origin annotations; a method that predicts flares and localizes the driving active region without such labels would be more efficient and interpretable.
AI.method: The authors propose Active Region attENtion Aggregation (ARENA), a neural network that aggregates over a variable number of active-region cutouts using a learned attention mechanism. It is trained via multiple-instance learning under weak supervision, requiring only an observation-level flare/no-flare label and no origin labels. The attention weights serve as a localization mechanism identifying the most relevant active region.
AI.result: ARENA achieves a Heidke skill score of 0.45, comparable to other flare prediction approaches. The learned attention provides interpretable localization of the driving active region without explicit annotations.
AI.conclusion: Active-region-based aggregation offers an efficient and interpretable approach to solar flare prediction, with weak supervision enabling both prediction and localization within a single architecture.

title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
summary: Molecular clouds exhibit complex, multi-scale dynamics driven by the interplay of turbulence, self-gravity, and gas pressure. Modelling these systems with conventional grid-based methods becomes increasingly expensive as spatial resolution and dimensionality increase. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free alternative by incorporating the governing equations directly into the training objective, but their ability to model realistic turbulent self-gravitating flows remains largely unexplored. We apply PINNs to isothermal molecular clouds initialized with astrophysically motivated turbulent velocity fields, considering subsonic and supersonic evolution in two and three dimensions. We benchmark the predicted density and velocity fields against the finite-volume code Athena++. PINNs accurately recover the global evolution of the flow over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, Mach numbers, and dimensionalities. Their training cost also exhibits weak dependence on spatial resolution, increasing by less than 25% from 128^3 to 1024^3 in our experiments. These results demonstrate that PINNs can model substantially more realistic self-gravitating turbulent flows than previously explored and provide a promising complementary framework for studying these systems.

AI.tldr: PINNs accurately model isothermal, self-gravitating turbulent molecular clouds in 2D and 3D, matching Athena++ on global evolution while showing weak resolution dependence (training cost rises <25% from 128³ to 1024³).
AI.motivation: Grid-based simulations of molecular clouds with turbulence, self-gravity, and gas pressure are computationally expensive as resolution and dimensionality grow, and PINNs' viability for realistic turbulent self-gravitating flows is largely unexplored.
AI.method: Mesh-free physics-informed neural networks trained on the governing equations, applied to isothermal clouds initialized with astrophysically motivated turbulent velocity fields (subsonic and supersonic, 2D and 3D), benchmarked against the finite-volume code Athena++.
AI.result: PINNs recover the global flow evolution over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, Mach numbers, and dimensionalities; training cost scales weakly with resolution, increasing under 25% from 128³ to 1024³.
AI.conclusion: PINNs can model substantially more realistic self-gravitating turbulent flows than previously shown, offering a promising complementary framework for studying molecular cloud dynamics.

title: One-Million-Year-Old Nascent Eclipsing Binaries in the LMC
summary: The light curves of nascent eclipsing binaries (EBs) feature sinusoidal reflection effects as a hot B-type main-sequence (MS) primary irradiates the near side of a cool, low-mass, pre-MS companion. We obtained multi-epoch echelle spectra with the MIKE spectrograph on the 6.5m Magellan-Clay Telescope of three nascent EBs embedded in H II regions within the LMC. By fitting atmospheric models to the spectra, the primaries are found to be mid-B dwarfs (T_eff,1 = 18,600-22,800 K; M_1 = 6.8-8.5 Msun). The dynamical masses of the secondaries are only M_2 = 0.38-0.95 Msun, yielding extremely small mass ratios q = M_2/M_1 = 0.05-0.11. Unlike solar-type primaries, which exhibit a dearth of close companions with q < 0.1 known as the brown dwarf desert, massive stars can readily form with very close companions below q < 0.1. By fitting PHOEBE models to the OGLE-III light curves, we measure the secondary radii R_2 = 2.0-2.8 Rsun and temperatures T_eff,2 = 4,000 K. The pre-MS companions are located high on the Hayashi track where evolutionary models indicate ages of only 1 Myr. Their extreme youth suggests that nascent EBs formed via inward disk migration during the previous embedded protostellar phase.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes three nascent eclipsing binaries (EBs) in LMC H II regions, finding mid-B dwarf primaries with extremely small mass ratios (q = 0.05–0.11) and pre-MS companions only ~1 Myr old, suggesting formation via inward disk migration.
AI.motivation: Solar-type primaries show a deficit of close companions with q < 0.1 (the brown dwarf desert), but whether massive stars share this companion deficiency is unclear. Nascent EBs hosting very low-mass pre-MS companions provide a direct probe of how such extreme mass-ratio binaries form.
AI.method: Multi-epoch echelle spectroscopy with the MIKE spectrograph on the 6.5 m Magellan-Clay Telescope of three nascent EBs in LMC H II regions was fitted with stellar atmosphere models to derive primary T_eff and masses. PHOEBE modeling of OGLE-III light curves yielded secondary radii and temperatures, and Hayashi-track evolutionary models constrained ages.
AI.result: Primaries are mid-B dwarfs (T_eff,1 = 18,600–22,800 K; M_1 = 6.8–8.5 Msun). Dynamical secondary masses are M_2 = 0.38–0.95 Msun, giving q = 0.05–0.11. Secondaries have R_2 = 2.0–2.8 Rsun and T_eff,2 ≈ 4,000 K, sitting high on the Hayashi track with ages of only ~1 Myr.
AI.conclusion: Unlike solar-type primaries, massive stars can readily form with very close, very low-mass (q < 0.1) companions, escaping the brown dwarf desert. The extreme youth indicates these nascent EBs formed via inward disk migration during the previous embedded protostellar phase.
